description:
This is a black-and-white photograph depicting an urban square in the early morning or late afternoon light, judging by the low position of the sun on the horizon. 

The scene is dominated by a cobblestone plaza, with several birds (likely pigeons or seagulls) scattered on the ground in the foreground, casting long shadows from the low sunlight. The reflective and irregular nature of the cobblestones captures and scatters the light, adding texture to the image.

In the midground, a group of people is seen walking or standing, some silhouetted against the bright sunlight. The human figures appear small, emphasizing the scale of the open square.

On each side of the photo are tall, dark building silhouettes. On the right-hand side, a church or similar historical building with a tower and spire rises above the rooftops, clearly visible against the sky. The left side features another large, indistinguishable structure. 

Above, the sky is partially clouded, with scattered birds in flight, adding a dynamic element to the otherwise calm and still composition. The entire image carries a moody and slightly nostalgic atmosphere due to the monochrome palette and the dramatic contrast between light and shadow.

The vantage point and the reference to "Adasia" (presumably a local nickname for a nearby statue or place) suggest this is a known viewpoint, possibly in a historic European city square. The perspective leads the viewer's eye directly toward the church tower and the vanishing point at the horizon, where the sun is either setting or rising.
